_theNoteYouFlagged.yourFinding: `washer-top-load` opened with a disproved ruling and carried its correction further down, so a skimming reader met the wrong claim first.
_theNoteYouFlagged.sweptNotPatched: Rule 13. Eight notes carry an appended correction; the sweep found only ONE whose leading claim is now false — the one you showed me. The other seven lead with statements still true.
_theNoteYouFlagged.theGeneralForm: Appending a correction to a note leaves the superseded claim in front. That is the Zone-Audit shape and F-29 §7b's shape, third instance, and this one was the design session's own. **A corrected note is authored whole, never appended** — the whole-file rule one level down. Applied here: the correction leads and the disproved reason is quoted inside it rather than standing alone.

_yourTwoCountCorrections: Both right and both the design session's. 22 not 21, 30 not 31 — a tally typed before the last correction landed, while `_expectedAfterMerge` was computed and correct. **Second instance in one day of restating a number that could have been derived**, which is the same lesson your PR #61 guard encodes.
_thirdQuestionNowAsked: Outside review's six misses all shared a shape: care that involves REMOVING or EMPTYING something. Every plumbing class was written asking three questions — what a trade does, what the household does, and what the owner removes, empties or clears. `trap-priming`, `drain-clearing`, `pump-basin-clearing` and `seasonal-drain-down` all come from the third.
_oneMoreSplitPointForTheSameReason: `float-and-switch-operation` is deliberately distinct from `float-and-pump-operation`, which is gated on a septic pump-out. A sump float is in the basement and can be looked at. Second instance of the same-check-different-reachability pattern recorded at `accessIsPerPointNotPerReference` — still handled by splitting the point rather than moving `access` onto the reference.

careCategories.label: Seasonal draining
careCategories.note: Standard hose bibs, irrigation, seasonal lines. Care that must happen before a date rather than on an interval — and the date is set by the weather, not the calendar.

careCategories.label: Trap priming
careCategories.note: Pouring water into a seldom-used drain so its trap does not dry and admit sewer gas. Household work, costs nothing, and nobody does it.

careCategories.label: Drain clearing
careCategories.note: Hair, grease and debris from an accessible trap or strainer — not a snaking job.

careCategories.label: Aerator and showerhead descaling
careCategories.note: Hard water in a limestone region. Household work with a visible result.

careCategories.label: Pump basin clearing
careCategories.note: Silt, gravel and debris from a sump or ejector basin. Cleared, the pump lasts; uncleared, the impeller does not.

inspectionPoints.label: Shutoff operation and labelling
inspectionPoints.note: Schedule caution: crusty old gate valves are NOT forced — note them for replacement and know the curb-stop fallback. The label matters as much as the valve, because the household reads it in an emergency.

inspectionPoints.label: Connector age and type
inspectionPoints.note: Braided stainless versus rubber, and how old. One of the highest water-damage risks in a house and it is answered by looking.

inspectionPoints.label: Static water pressure
inspectionPoints.note: A pressure reducing valve fails silently and high pressure destroys fixtures, appliances and softener resin. This measurement is the only thing that catches it.

inspectionPoints.label: Flush and refill behaviour
inspectionPoints.note: A running fill valve is the commonest silent water cost in a house, and on a well it is also a pump running all night.

inspectionPoints.label: Trap holding water
inspectionPoints.note: A dried floor-drain trap admits sewer gas and it is invisible until somebody smells it.

inspectionPoints.label: Float and switch operation
inspectionPoints.note: Deliberately distinct from `float-and-pump-operation`, which is gated on a septic pump-out. A sump float is in the basement and can be looked at — the same distinction that split `condensate-pump-operation` out.

inspectionPoints.label: Check valve function
inspectionPoints.note: Backflow makes a healthy pump cycle repeatedly. The pump gets replaced and the check valve stays.

inspectionPoints.label: Discharge line and termination
inspectionPoints.note: Blockage, disconnection, and freezing solid in a Quinte winter — a discharge that freezes makes the pump run against a closed pipe.

inspectionPoints.label: Automatic valve exercise record
inspectionPoints.note: A motorised shutoff that has never closed may not close. Most exercise themselves on a schedule and report it; the record is what says so.

inspectionPoints.label: Tap type and seasonal drainage
inspectionPoints.note: Frost-free or standard is the whole of the split, and getting it wrong in October splits a pipe inside the wall.

opportunityConditions.label: High static pressure with no reducing valve
Rubber supply connectors in use
opportunityConditions.note: Cheap to replace, and the failure is a flooded house rather than a drip.

opportunityConditions.label: Water-supplied fixture with no leak detection
Sump pump with no backup
opportunityConditions.note: A power cut and a wet spring arrive together more often than not.

opportunityConditions.label: No backwater valve where one is warranted
Shutoff present but unlabelled
opportunityConditions.note: The §1 emergency sheet is the deliverable this feeds, and an unlabelled valve is one the household will not find at 2am.

opportunityConditions.label: Window well with no cover or blocked drain

ownerQuestions.label: Do you know where the main water shutoff is?
ownerQuestions.note: The single most useful thing a household can know, and the §1 emergency sheet exists because most do not.

ownerQuestions.label: Has the basement ever taken water?
Does anything drip, run or refill on its own?
ownerQuestions.note: Households hear a running toilet for months and do not report it, because it is not broken.

ownerQuestions.label: Do you drain the outside taps in the fall?

classes.label: Main water shutoff
classes.note: The §1 emergency sheet depends on this one. Its exercise carries the schedule's caution — an old gate valve is not forced, it is noted for replacement, and the curb stop is the fallback.

classes.label: Curb stop
classes.note: The municipal fallback when the interior valve fails, and it needs a key and usually a call. Documenting where it is costs nothing and is worth a great deal once. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Frost-free outdoor tap
classes.note: Must NOT be drained down — the split from the standard tap is that the correct winter action is opposite, and a hose left attached defeats it entirely.

classes.label: Outdoor tap
classes.note: Must be drained before freezing. Getting the type wrong in October splits a pipe inside the wall, which is why v0.2 split these.

classes.label: Sink
classes.note: Kitchen and bathroom merged per §1.2 — identical care, identical inspection.

classes.label: Toilet
classes.note: Its whole risk is a fill valve that runs and a supply connector that fails, and both are answered by looking rather than by doing. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Floor drain
classes.note: The classic unnoticed one: the trap dries and admits sewer gas, invisible until somebody smells it. Priming is household work, costs nothing, and nobody does it. No replacement horizon — a floor drain is part of the slab.

classes.label: Drain cleanout
classes.note: Inspected for presence and access, never maintained. No horizon — it is a fitting in the drain line. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Backwater valve
classes.note: Access-found: it lives under a floor cover that may or may not be findable. Its flap is inspected when the cover is off. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Sump pump
classes.note: The schedule keys on `sump-pump` with eight items across eight cadences — the densest house-grain coverage in the file. This class adds the object-grain half.

classes.label: Backup sump pump
classes.note: Battery or water-powered, and the battery is a consumable with its own lifespan — which is the split from the primary.

classes.label: Sewage ejector pump
classes.note: Different job, different failure, same config type — and its failure is sewage rather than groundwater, which is why it is not merged.

classes.label: Sump check valve
classes.note: Backflow makes a healthy pump cycle repeatedly. The pump gets replaced and the check valve stays, which is the failure this class exists to name. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Sump discharge line
classes.note: Blockage, disconnection, and freezing solid in a Quinte winter — a frozen discharge makes the pump run against a closed pipe until it burns out. No horizon: it is corrected, not replaced on a lifespan. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Leak sensor
classes.note: The schedule keys on `leak-sensor` for review; this adds placement and power, which is where they actually fail — a sensor on a shelf above the floor detects nothing.

classes.label: Automatic water shutoff
classes.note: One detects, one acts — and the one that acts has a valve that seizes. Its exercise record is the only evidence it still closes. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Gas shutoff
classes.note: Inspected and labelled, never operated. HouseSteady labour cannot touch gas at all, per the owner 2026-08-05, and exercising a gas valve is not an exception to that. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Pressure reducing valve
classes.note: Flagged by all three outside reviewers at v0.2 and they were right. It fails silently and high pressure destroys fixtures, appliances and softener resin — and a measurement is the only thing that catches it. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Appliance water connector
classes.note: Washer, dishwasher, toilet and fridge hoses. One of the highest water-damage risks in a house, answered entirely by looking at what type they are and how old. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Window well
classes.note: The well, its cover and its drain — a frequent route for unnoticed basement water. No horizon: a well is a hole with a liner.

_modifiedClasses.label: Top-load washer
_modifiedClasses.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-05 by outside review, and this correction leads because the claim it replaces should not be read first. The class originally declared zero care with a stated reason — that a top-loader has no gasket to dry and no drum cycle to run. The reason was wrong: a top-loader runs a tub-clean cycle and many carry a pump trap. **A ruling with a reason is harder to catch than an omission**, because it looks considered; neither internal pass found it. Its remaining risk is still the supply line, which is inspection.

_howToApply: Append the five arrays. Then REPLACE each entry in `_modifiedClasses` by id — 1 class, change confined to `note`.
